subject: basic plot of all independent variables and regression stats

messages.author: e3f242bd4e6a7ccd
messages.subject: basic plot of all independent variables and regression stats
parts:
I was recently told about ggplot and have been looking into it. I'm an
epidemiologist and not a statistician and just starting using R about
2 years ago.

I have two questions.

First, one of the first things I like to do is to simply plot out the
univariate distributions of each variable. For most of my studies,
this is easy as there are not that many variables and I do them one by
one. But I am now involved in a study with many many variables and I
just think there must be an easy way to do this in R. I was looking
through ggplot and know about facet_grid, but that seems to just
subset the data of one variable. I want to just have each panel as a
simple distribution. It would be the graphic equivalent of summary
(data.frame). Does ggplot do this? If not, do you know of another
package? I tried lattice but couldn't get that to work either.

Second, I like to print out the regression stats on my graphs. I
figured out how to plot the regression line on the graph (i used lm
but this should be applicable to anything), but I can't find anything
in the help file about printing out the actual r-squared, equation, p-
value, etc onto the graph. Now, I could just add text to the plot, but
I was thinking that if ggplot calculated the regression line, the
results have to be stored somewhere and are probably easy to include
with some option.

I tried the search feature in the discussion group but was
unsuccessful. Thanks for your help.

Ian

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: basic plot of all independent variables and regression stats
parts:
Not precisely what you're looking for, but you might want to check out
the "ezCor()" function in the "ez" package:
install.packages('ez',type='source')
library('ez')
?ezCor

See the example in the ezCor() help for demonstration for using it. If
you want something similar but different, see the source (simply type
'ezCor' at the prompt) to see how it was all put together.

messages.author: ba9318fcb03a20d0
messages.subject: Re: basic plot of all independent variables and regression stats
parts:
Hi Ian,
If you have a large number of variables, where if you try to plot all
densities
it would take many pages, you should look at the Hmisc package.
for instance
> library(Hmisc)
> latex(describe(<your data.frame>))
will give you output to latex, and with pdflatex you get something like
this
http://biostat.mc.vanderbilt.edu/wiki/pub/Main/Hmisc/counties.pdf

Hope this helps
Nicholas

messages.subject: Re: basic plot of all independent variables and regression stats
parts:
Hi,
You need to have a full (la)tex system installed. If you are on windows,
install miktex. If you are on a debian based linux system
sudo apt-get install texlive

On an rpm based linux system like fedora, probably something like
yum install texlive
but not sure

Mac: on your own ;)

The two packages should be part of texlive, and miktex has an automatic
package installer.

Hope this helps

Nicholas
